name: Trello
description: Trello is a visual work management product built around boards, lists, and cards. Teams use it to organize projects, track work through stages, assign people, record due dates, and discuss tasks.
agentUseSummary: Connect a Trello account once, then select which agents may find and read boards and cards, prepare card changes, create or update cards, and add comments under Safe or Dangerous policy.

capabilities.label: View boards
capabilities.description: List bounded boards available to the connected member.

capabilities.label: Find and read cards
capabilities.description: Find bounded cards and read one explicit card with limited context.

capabilities.label: Prepare card changes
capabilities.description: Prepare an exact card create, update, or comment locally without changing Trello.

capabilities.label: Create, update, and comment
capabilities.description: Create or update one card and add one bounded comment.

allowed.label: List boards
allowed.description: List a bounded set of boards available to the connected member.

allowed.label: List board cards
allowed.description: List a bounded set of open cards on one explicit board.

allowed.label: Read a card
allowed.description: Read one explicit card with bounded comments and member context.

allowed.label: Find cards
allowed.description: Find a bounded set of cards matching an explicit query.

allowed.label: Prepare a card change
allowed.description: Prepare and hash one card create, update, or comment locally.

approvalRequired.label: Create a card
approvalRequired.description: Create one card in an explicit list; Safe mode requires matching approval.

approvalRequired.label: Update a card
approvalRequired.description: Update bounded fields on one explicit card; Safe mode requires matching approval.

approvalRequired.label: Comment on a card
approvalRequired.description: Add one bounded comment to an explicit card; Safe mode requires matching approval.

blocked.label: Administer Trello
blocked.description: Workspace, member, Power-Up, webhook, enterprise, and billing administration are outside V1.

blocked.label: Delete Trello data
blocked.description: Board, list, card, checklist, label, and comment deletion are outside V1.

blocked.label: Call arbitrary Trello endpoints
blocked.description: Raw paths, batch requests, unbounded pagination, and arbitrary REST calls are never exposed to agents.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Bounded reads and local drafts run directly; each Trello card write requires matching approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Every selected Trello operation supported by this connector runs without Relay per-action approval; connection ownership, Trello-granted access, request bounds, audits, redaction, and provider limits still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts eight typed Trello tools and attaches the authorized member token server-side without exposing it to the agent.
Railway mounts eight typed Trello tools and attaches the authorized member token server-side without exposing it to the agent.

providerSetup.blocker: Relay Console's Trello Power-Up, API key and OAuth secret, exact production callback, read/write permissions, allowed origin, branding, and a fresh production authorization have not been configured and verified.
providerSetup.nextAction: Create the Relay Console Trello Power-Up, generate its API key and secret, register https://api.relayconsole.work as an allowed origin and the exact callback, add TRELLO_API_KEY and TRELLO_API_SECRET to Railway, then verify request-token signing, member and Workspace binding, bounded reads, Safe writes, Dangerous writes, revocation, disconnect, and denial.

evidence.supports: Trello documents delegated API-key authorization, basic OAuth 1.0 request, authorize, and access-token endpoints, the application signing secret, read/write scopes, allowed origins, callback behavior, secret user tokens, and token revocation.
Trello documents Power-Up API keys, member tokens, boards, lists, cards, actions and comments, search, nested resources, and bounded pagination.
The core Trello REST reference documents board, card, member, search, token, and webhook resources and states that Forge and Atlassian OAuth2 apps cannot access these core resources.
Trello documents per-key, per-token, member-route, search-route, database-time, and response-size limits plus HTTP 429 responses and rate-limit headers.
